content:
Hey! Wondering if there's interest in formalizing classical integrable systems, methods like, Lax pairs, Bethe-ansatz-style techniques, and using them to reframe results already in PhysLib from an integrability point of view.

Two concrete examples already in the library: the simple pendulum and Kepler's two-body problem. Both are classically integrable, and showing that explicitly (conserved quantities in involution, action-angle variables, etc.) feels like a natural addition on top of what's already there.

Does this seem like a good direction? Would it fit as its own area, or should it live alongside the existing classical mechanics results?

This could also extend to the QFT and String Theory spaces (but will require a little more work :sweat_smile: ).

I think this is great area! It should likely sit alongside the existing classical mechanic results, but I don't think it should subsume the traditional approaches to these problems (someone should still be able to look at these problems and understand them without knowing integrable systems).
